instructions: See docs/ratings.md. Give every season a rating on the absolute scale. Rate the player that season, never their career.

seasons.note: A World Cup winner in a Chelsea side that conceded 30; rated at the Pallister anchor — good, occasionally elite, and error-prone.
Thirty-two, and a season away from Marseille; the passing was undimmed, the pace that covered for his risk-taking was not.
Thirty-three starts as first-choice centre-half in a Newcastle side that finished fourth; his best season.
Sixteen starts; a season broken up by an achilles problem, not a decline in ability.
Twenty-one league goals in his last United season; the finishing was untouched, and it was the relationship with the manager rather than the ability that ended it.
Twenty, signed in January, and already an aggressive, front-footed defender who would start in the Premier League for a decade.
A first full season as a starter, and immediately the more reliable half of the partnership.
The centre-half of a side that finished fourth; brave, well organised, and still short of pace against a runner.
Thirty, and a back-up at Sunderland after relegation with Derby; four starts.
Eighteen, played out of position at left-back, and still the quickest and most direct player on the pitch at times. Rated on evident top-flight ability, not on output.
Nineteen, and already the most inventive player in the side.
A first full season as an attacking wide man rather than a full-back: five goals and six assists for a side that created almost nothing else.
PFA Team of the Year in Wigan first top-flight season, and the best right-back in the division that year outside the top four.
A January loan who was immediately the best passer in a side that finished fourth. Half a season, but the quality was unmistakable.
Nine goals and nine assists from midfield for a sixth-placed Everton; the best season of his career and clearly above the Barry anchor.
Eleven starts on the way back from a cruciate injury; six goals says the delivery survived, the eleven starts say the legs had not yet.
Thirty-five, three starts, and three seasons after his last regular top-flight football; a passing midfielder with nothing left physically.
Two seasons in Spain in between; back at City at 27 as a twelve-start squad forward, the awkward brilliance intact and the sharpness gone.
Ten league goals from left-back, most of them penalties; a fearsome left foot and a genuinely hard defender, with obvious discipline and mobility limits.
The knee finally gave out; nine starts and retirement at 30.
Seven starts and one goal after a January arrival from River Plate; the struggle was settling, not ability.
Eight starts in a season interrupted by injury and a family bereavement.
Thirty, four goals, and a move to New York already agreed; the movement was intact but the sharpness in front of goal had gone.
Five starts — injury and a falling-out with Roy Evans, not a drop in ability.
Recalled by England for Euro 96 at 31; the best of his Liverpool seasons.
Joined Manchester City in March 1994.
Bradford’s main creative outlet in a survival season, at 33; still an honest lower-half winger.
Thirty-four, nine starts, and relegation with Bradford; the crossing was still the only thing about him above the level.
Thirty-nine and an ever-present for a Forest side that conceded 69; a competent shot-stopper a long way below modern standard.
Ten league goals from seventeen starts in his first Chelsea season; the touch and the link play were already the best parts of his game.
Twelve league goals in a title-winning side while spending much of the season dropping off the front to link play; a genuinely elite second striker.
Sixteen starts and two goals in a title-winning side built around Drogba; the link play was as good as ever, the goals were not his to score.
Thirty, on loan at Spurs after Barcelona and Monaco had each moved him on; a long way from the Chelsea forward of four years earlier.
An ever-present in the back four that kept Stoke up on their return; overwhelming in both boxes and comfortable with nothing else asked of him.
A fractured skull in 1996 and a chronic knee problem; a bit-part player at 35.
Seven goals in nineteen starts that kept West Ham up almost single-handedly; the ability was already close to elite before the output caught up.
Twenty-three league goals as the whole of a City attack that had not yet been built around anyone else.
In and out of the side after injury and a change of manager; the ability was unchanged.
Three years at Celtic in between, including a Scottish Player of the Year award; he came back a better midfielder.
Eleven starts and relegation with Derby at 29; the last of his top-flight football.
Ever-present and the most consistent defender at the club that season; the ceiling was still a good lower-half left-back.
A near ever-present at 22 and called up by England; dominant in the air, limited on the turn.
Eight league goals from centre-half, nearly all headers, in an Everton side that finished fifth; the England call-up that followed was deserved.
Seventeen starts and an unhappy first season after the move; the player was the same, the settled place in a back four was not.
Thirty-six years old and a first-choice centre-half for a promoted side; reading and positioning entirely compensating for the pace that had gone.
The season Ferguson picked him against every good midfield in Europe; energy, positional sense and use of the ball all at their peak.
